device.name: TacEx Ball Rolling (Isaac Lab privileged task)

facts.text: TacEx-Ball-Rolling-Privileged-v0 is registered with entry_point tacex_tasks.ball_rolling_privileged.base_env:BallRollingEnv and disable_env_checker=True
BallRollingEnv is an Isaac Lab DirectRLEnv subclass configured by BallRollingEnvCfg
The cfg sets decimation to 1 and sim.dt to 0.01 s, so one environment step advances 10 ms
The environment computes its step interval as sim.dt times decimation
The configured episode length is 8.3333 / 2 s; the source comment calls it 500 timesteps, but at dt 0.01 s the quotient is about 416.7
The action space has five components (dx, dy, dz, droll, dpitch); dyaw is omitted
Every action component is clamped to [-1, 1] before it is passed to the IK controller
The differential IK controller is configured for pose commands in relative mode with the damped least squares method
The observation space has 14 values: 3 for the end-effector position, 2 for its roll and pitch, 2 for the goal, 2 for the object position and 5 for the actions
The observation concatenates the end-effector position, its roll and pitch, the object xy position, the desired goal xy position and the five actions
The success reward has weight 10 and a 0.005 m object-goal threshold
The reward adds the success term when the object-goal distance is below success_reward['threshold']
The ball is spawned at (0.5, 0, 0.01) m
The ball radius is 0.005 m
The object bounds are x in (0.225, 0.75) m and y in (-0.375, 0.375) m, and too_far_away_threshold is 0.35 m
An episode ends when the object leaves the configured x or y bounds, is more than 1 m from the goal, or is farther from the end effector than the configured too_far_away_threshold
obj_pos_randomization_range lists [-0.1, 0.1] per axis in its first entry and [-0.25, 0.25] in its second
The reset sets the goal to the object default position plus a uniform offset in each axis, using the obj_pos_randomization_range entry indexed by curriculum_phase_id
The robot is the Franka Panda arm with a GelSight Mini sensor and stiff PD control
The cfg runs 1024 environments in parallel by default
TacEx requires Isaac Sim 4.5 and Isaac Lab 2.1.1; the installation was tested on Ubuntu 22.04 with a 4090 GPU
The local installation requires Isaac Sim 4.5 and Isaac Lab 2.1.1 on Ubuntu 22.04

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 resets the fake's Python random.Random and fixes the goal draw, and the kinematic update is deterministic; the upstream seed controls Isaac Lab's generators and the sample_uniform goal draw, and the two were not compared because the upstream stack was not run

gaps: kinematic F0 stand-in with no dynamics: no Isaac Sim rigid-body or contact physics, no friction, mass, IK solver, joint limits, Franka arm or actuator model; the ball follows the end effector kinematically instead of being pushed by contact forces
the fake's end-effector start pose, push gain and contact radius are placeholders; the upstream start state comes from the Franka default joint positions and the differential IK controller
only the success term of the reward is modelled (base_env.py:480); the reaching, tracking, orientation, height, action-rate and joint-velocity terms of the sum are omitted

the tactile, RGB and depth sensors and the rendering pipeline of TacEx are not modelled; this driver binds the privileged 14-value scalar observation, not the vision or tactile observation groups of the RGB, depth, Taxim-FOTS or UIPC tasks

the end-effector orientation and the goal height are held at zero in the fake, while the upstream observation carries the computed roll and pitch and the goal has a fixed z of 0.00125 m (base_env.py:270)

the truncation step is the fake's floor of episode_length_s / dt (416); the upstream comment on base_env.py:222 says 500 timesteps and the rounding happens in Isaac Lab's DirectRLEnv outside the clone, so the real count was not verified
the upstream environment is vectorized over 1024 environments by default (base_env.py:100) while the MHS Gymnasium bridge drives one environment

the upstream stack (Isaac Sim 4.5, Isaac Lab 2.1.1, Linux, an NVIDIA GPU) was never started here, so the sim backend was not run; the upstream tasks are built with gym.make(task_name, cfg=env_cfg) and the cfg cannot be constructed without that stack
the fake draws goals with Python's random.Random while the upstream uses Isaac Lab's sample_uniform on the simulator device, so one seed does not give the same goal on both
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair, and the bridge reports snapshot_restore false
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep, so simulated time advances only with steps

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
